sections.title: The Independent Watchdog
sourceHeadings: Slide 15: The Independent Watchdog
sections.body:
**LSI** means low-speed internal oscillator; it runs independently if software stops. A **prescaler** divides its clock; **reload** sets timeout.

IWDG at 0x40003000 runs from independent nominal 32 kHz LSI. KR low 16 bits: 0xCCCC starts, 0x5555 unlocks, 0xAAAA refreshes.

PR bits 2:0=3 divide the clock by 32. RLR bits 11:0=999 gives 1000 ticks at 1 kHz, nominal 1 s.

Poll SR PVU 0/RVU 1/WVU 2 to zero with a bound, then refresh every 250 ms. WINR bits 11:0 is unused.

Once started only reset stops it. DBG APBFZ1 DBG_IWDG_STOP freezes it during debugging.

LSI varies with voltage/temperature, motivating 4× refresh margin. Wokwi does not implement IWDG.

| Step | Write | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `KR = 0xCCCC` | start (also switches the LSI on) |
| 2 | `KR = 0x5555` | unlock `PR` and `RLR` |
| 3 | `PR = 3`, `RLR = 999` | 32 000 / 32 = 1000 counts/s; 1000 counts |
| 4 | wait `SR == 0`, **bounded** | values cross into the LSI clock domain |
| 5 | `KR = 0xAAAA` | refresh — and every 250 ms after |

| Register / function | Width, value and bit fields |
|---|---|
| KR  —  0xCCCC start, 0x5555 unlock, 0xAAAA refresh | 32; 15:0 KEY |
| PR  —  /32: 32 kHz -> 1 kHz | 32 = 0x00000003; 2:0 PR |
| RLR  —  999 + 1 counts = 1.000 s | 32 = 0x000003E7; 11:0 RL |
| SR  —  update in progress, polled to 0 | 32; 2 WVU, 1 RVU, 0 PVU |
| WINR  —  window: never written by wdog.c | 32; 11:0 WIN |

Use `DBG->APBFZ1.DBG_IWDG_STOP` for GDB breakpoints without watchdog reset.

LSI is separate from the 48 MHz system clock. Four refreshes per nominal timeout give more margin than a near-one ratio such as 1.1.

sections.title: Heartbeats, Not a Single Kick
sourceHeadings: Slide 16: Heartbeats, Not a Single Kick
sections.body:
Each task owns a heartbeat counter. **Preemption** pauses lower-priority work; shared bitmap updates can lose another task’s progress.

Low-priority health feeds IWDG only if input, app, display and telemetry counters all advanced.

Display missing is bit 2 or 0b0100. Shared alive bits can lose read-modify-write updates under preemption, while separate single-writer counters cannot.

If a higher-priority task spins, health also starves and hardware refresh stops.

sections.title: Failsafes — Defined Behaviour for Every Fault
sourceHeadings: Slide 17: Failsafes — Defined Behaviour for Every Fault
sections.body:
**NACK** means the device did not acknowledge. **Dirty pages** await display transfer. **NVIC** is the interrupt controller, also used for software reset.

Fault responses are defined in the table: absent OLED skips flush, ADC failure preserves buttons with zero axes, hung tasks stop beats, and I²C errors preserve dirty pages for retry. Bounded scan/waits prevent bus hangs.

Wokwi lacks IWDG, so running health uses NVIC reset 1.5 s after last feed. Spinning priority 5 input starves that fallback forever.

CSR2 reset flags are read at boot then cleared via RMVF 23.

| Fault | What the template does | Shown by |
|---|---|---|
| OLED absent (NACK at 0x3C) | banner says so; display skips the flush, everything else runs | banner |
| ADC fails to start | `pad_init()` < 0: buttons still work, stick/knob read 0 | banner |
| a task **hangs** (`hang display`) | its beats stop → `health` prints who, stops refreshing → IWDG reset ≤ 1.0 s | `health`, LD4 stops |
| a task **spins** (`spin input`) | everything below it starves, `health` included → IWDG reset | screen and shell freeze |
| no IWDG (Wokwi) | `health` still alive 1.5 s after the last refresh → `NVIC_SystemReset()` | serial monitor |
| I²C error | counted in `i2c_errors`, reported in `$SYS` and `stats`; `oled.c` keeps the page dirty, so the next flush retries it | `$SYS` |
| bus stuck | `scan` stops at the first timeout; every wait in `i2c.c` is bounded (lesson 09) | `scan` |
| reset of any kind | `RCC->CSR2` read at boot, cause printed, flags cleared with `RMVF` | banner |

| Register / function | Width, value and bit fields |
|---|---|
| CSR2  —  reset cause | 32; 31 LPWRRSTF, 30 WWDGRSTF, 29 IWDGRSTF, 28 SFTRSTF, 27 PWRRSTF, 26 PINRSTF, 25 OBLRSTF, 23 RMVF, 1 LSIRDY, 0 LSION |

sections.title: The Timing Budget
sourceHeadings: Slide 18: The Timing Budget
sections.body:
**Bus load** is transfer-time fraction. Polled transfers also occupy CPU. **Baud** is serial symbols/second; **HUD** is on-screen status.

Measured full-frame bytes are 1088. At 400 kHz and 9 clocks/byte this implies 24.5 ms×20 Hz, giving 49% bus/polled CPU load.

APP uses at most 35 wire bytes at 10 Hz, about 3% of 115200 baud, with 29-byte max measured body. ADC about 21 µs, app below 1% and switches below 1% are estimates.

Border/HUD redraw dirties all eight pages even when still. Label estimates in design review and replace them with measurements in the report.

| Item | Per run | Rate | Load | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OLED flush, all 8 pages | 1088 B × 22.5 µs = **24.5 ms** | 20 Hz | **49 % of the I²C bus, polled → CPU** | bytes **measured on the host**; 9 clocks/byte at 400 kHz |
| `$APP` frame | ≤ 35 B on the wire | 10 Hz | 3 % of 115 200 baud | longest body **measured on the host**: 29 B |
| `pad_read()` | 3 ADC conversions, ~21 µs | 100 Hz | ~0.2 % (estimate) | lesson 09: ~7 µs per conversion |
| `app_step()` (steer) | integer only | 50 Hz | < 1 % (estimate) | measure: `stats` → `app` resp |
| context switches | a few µs each | ~400/s | < 1 % (estimate) | `os_switches()` in `$SYS` |

sections.title: The Memory Budget
sourceHeadings: Slide 19: The Memory Budget
sections.body:
**Flash** holds code; **RAM** holds data/stacks. A **high-water mark** is maximum observed stack depth. Include library call chains.

The table itemises build memory: stacks, framebuffer, rings, stdio and reserved heap/main stack.

Printing alone can need about 650 B of call-chain stack, including 144 B _vfprintf_r and 64 B _printf_i frames. Static stack estimates need full-demo high-water confirmation with ≤75% used.

Around 2 KB remains: a second 1 KB framebuffer is judged unsuitable with required margins, while a 64-entry replay log can fit.

| Item | Bytes | |
|---|---|---|
| **FLASH total** | **16 576** | of 32 768 (50.6 %) |
| **RAM total** | **10 280** | of 12 288 (83.7 %) |
| six task stacks | 6 016 | 160 + 256 + 288 + 224 + 256 + 320 words |
| idle stack | 256 | the kernel's |
| OLED framebuffer | 1 032 | 8 × (1 + 128) |
| UART rings | 320 | TX 256 + RX 64 |
| newlib stdio | 388 | `__sf` + `_impure_data` |
| heap + main stack | 1 536 | `link.ld`'s minimum reservation |

sections.title: Measuring on the Target — `stats`
sourceHeadings: Slide 20: Measuring on the Target — `stats`
sections.body:
**Response** is wake-to-completion time, including preemption. Sampled CPU percentage alone cannot prove deadline compliance.

stats reports sampled 1 kHz CPU%, exact stack high-water, period/runs, wake-to-done average/peak response, ms-resolution late count and missed-period over count. Use peak response to check deadlines.

Owner-handled reset requests delimit each reporting interval. TIM14 PSC 47 gives 1 MHz;16-bit differences survive one wrap and spans up to 65 ms, while TIM3 and SysTick remain occupied by sound/kernel.

| Column | Comes from | Exact? |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu%` | the kernel's per-task tick count (`os_task_t.ticks`) | **sampled** at 1 kHz — fair over seconds |
| `stack used/size` | `os_stack_used()`: untouched `0xDEADBEEF` words | exact high-water mark |
| `resp avg/max` | TIM14 at 1 MHz, wake → done | exact; **includes preemption** |
| `late` | `os_ticks()` at wake − due tick | ms resolution |
| `over` | runs whose response exceeded the period | a missed deadline |

```text
task     pri  cpu%   stack used/size   period  runs  resp avg/max us  late  over
```

The timer derivation is 48 MHz/(47+1)=1 MHz.

sections.title: What Was Measured — and What Could Not Be
sourceHeadings: Slide 27: What Was Measured — and What Could Not Be
sections.body:
Build, simulation and silicon observations support different claims. Host health checks do not prove a physical watchdog reset.

The evidence table distinguishes build measurements, host app/health/frame tests, static stack analysis and unmeasured CPU/idle/response. IWDG code matches ST source/header but was not executed, and Wokwi cannot demonstrate its silicon reset.

First target observations should be boot banner, stats after a minute and hang display/software reset. Host checks establish health logic.

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| builds with zero warnings, 16 576 B flash, 10 280 B RAM | this lesson's build |
| app logic: speeds, friction stop, fuzz, determinism, bot score | **measured on the host** — the related topic |
| health logic: missing bitmap, starve and force times | **measured on the host** — `[8]` |
| frame cost 1088 B | **measured on the host** — byte count through the real `oled.c` |
| stack sizes | static: `-fstack-usage` + disassembly; **not run** |
| CPU %, response times, idle | **not measured** — needs the target: `stats` |
| IWDG register sequence | ST's HAL source and header; **not run anywhere** |
| IWDG reset on silicon | **not observable in Wokwi** (not implemented there) |

The proposed Wokwi hang-display observation expects the software fallback reset around 1.5 s after the last refresh.

sections.title: What Carries Forward
sourceHeadings: Slide 28: What Carries Forward
sections.body:
**RTOS** means real-time operating system; **UART** is asynchronous serial communication. **Debouncing** rejects switch chatter. Ownership and safety rules transfer to other products.

The template combines debouncing, TIM3/TIM14, RTOS, UART framing, I²C, watchdog and OLED. Portable app_step/control_step interfaces preserve host-testable logic when hardware changes.

Numeric requirements, explicit ownership, measured budgets and honest fault limits are recurring product-engineering habits.
